affectedPublicSurfaces: the release path for api.app-juli.com: no candidate instance may start until pending schema changes are proven additive

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: local gate execution against fixture migrations; no candidate instance and no public traffic are involved in proving the gate itself

journeys.name: additive-change-passes
journeys.entryUrl: local: gate run against a fixture migration adding a nullable column and a new table
assertions: the additive change is permitted to proceed to candidate start

journeys.name: destructive-change-refused
journeys.entryUrl: local: fixture migrations dropping a column, renaming a table, and narrowing a type
assertions: each is refused with the offending change named in output
the gate exits non-zero and is a hard block, not a warning
no candidate instance is started after a refusal

journeys.name: data-moving-change-refused
journeys.entryUrl: local: fixture migration executing a data backfill or row rewrite
assertions: the data-moving migration is refused from automatic release
the refusal names the statement that moved data

htmlRoutes: not-applicable: the migration gate has no HTML route or static assets

migrationCompatibility.notes: The slice adds the gate that enforces additive-only change; it introduces no migration of its own. Additivity is what makes code rollback safe while two versions share one database, which is why this is a hard block rather than advisory. Migrations are never automatically reverted.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: revert the commit; the gate is additive to the existing safe-alembic pipeline and removing it restores the prior behaviour exactly

doNotInfer: replacing or bypassing the existing safe-alembic pipeline and its allowlist — extend them
running the gate against the production database; it inspects pending migration definitions
candidate slot, traffic-switch, or rollback wiring — those are #838 through #840
